Prime Letter Cipher

A=1 … Z=26  ·  HI → p18 × p29 for two random primes

Encode a word

Each letter gets its own random prime, raised to the letter's number. The encoded number is the product of all of them.

Letters A–Z only. No spaces or punctuation.
Base 10 is ordinary decimal. Bases above 10 use the letters A–Z as extra digits.
Primes come from your browser's cryptographic random generator and are checked with Miller–Rabin.
Encoded number
LetterValueRandom primeFactorFactor size

The primes are random, so the number keeps which letters you used but not their order. The decoder recovers the letters and then searches for every word they can spell.

Decode a number

Factors the number on every CPU core, turns each exponent back into a letter, then checks the letters against 1.1 million words, names and places in seven languages, every arrangement of the letters, and the words hidden inside them.

Spaces, commas and line breaks are ignored. In base 10 you can also type a product such as 1009^12 × 2003^5.
